conclusion: Five of six preregistered SWE-bench Verified entries recount to the integer from their own archived per-instance logs (265, 359, 384, 388, 396), agree on all twelve per-repository sub-counts each, and show zero self-consistency failures across 2,484 reports re-derived from the test results recorded in the same file. The sixth answers none of its 500 documented log keys, and an archive-wide three-key probe finds 15 of 134 entries with no per-instance report at the documented location, so the reproducible thing here is the arithmetic and the fragile thing is the evidence's retrievability.
confidence: High for the recount and self-consistency verdicts on the five recountable units: the arithmetic is exact integer counting over files fetched with recorded ETags and byte counts, it is cross-checked against a second published artifact at 12-way grain, and four planted faults were each shown to turn the verdict they should turn and leave the other alone. Medium for the availability findings: anonymous ListBucket returns 403, so 'absent' always means 'absent at the documented key' and never 'absent from the bucket', and for 13 of the 15 unreachable entries the format-migration reading is inference, not measurement. The no_logs and no_generation discrepancies rest on our reading of what those two fields mean; the underlying counts do not.
